quote: surface: a principal act, a device seat's room act, an install or an
problem: Principal surface refuses and counts every device seat's room act that comes from a process the harness starts. Device seat and Personal room exempt only the personal room's create room act, which is recorded 'at ParleyInn's first start there'. After a plugin or managed install, that first start is a hook handler or the MCP server, so read together the personal room is never created and runs' events have no seat to go to. 'ParleyInn's first start' is also never defined.
fix: Append to the refusal: "but for the create room act of its node's personal room, which the first core component to run on the node records (Personal room)", and say which component that is.

quote: than ParleyInn's own hook handlers, MCP server and harness strip, is recall: never
problem: A hook call from inside a run's tool process is refused (Hook). Nothing says the same for `parinn status --line` or `parinn mcp` run from a run's tool process. An agent can therefore call the harness strip itself and get Health output back without an envelope, against I2 and against 'what it returns is enveloped'. Implementers will also recognise the exemption differently.
fix: Add: "A harness-strip or MCP-server call from inside a run's tool process is recall (enveloped), just as a hook call from one is refused and counted."

quote: Managed policy and repository configuration each override the
problem: The candidate never says what happens to a value in managed policy or repository configuration that is not cut-only. Ignoring it silently breaks I6. Ignoring a managed value also conflicts with 'ParleyInn never overrides it (I7)'. Implementers will choose differently.
fix: Add: "A value in managed policy or repository configuration that is not cut-only is not applied; it is counted and shown on Setup (I6), and ParleyInn never rewrites the policy itself."

quote: `parinn uninstall` records the widening act turning capture off before it
problem: Uninstall can also run through the harness's plugin path or the managed install path, where no principal act can be recorded. Recording then stops with no capture-off act and no capture gap. No install path records capture back on either, so after reinstalling, the record still says capture is off and implementers will differ on whether the hook handlers record.
fix: Add: "An uninstall outside a principal surface records no act, and its runs show `unrecorded`; `parinn install` at a principal surface records turning capture on while capture is off."

quote: This node's hook handlers recording its runs' events.
problem: Capture covers only the hook handlers. Nothing says whether `parinn ingest`, including one an agent's tool process runs as recall, may append a witnessed run's events while capture is off. The capture-gap marker then moves the ingest position past those events and shows a gap that may already be recorded, so I1's exception is stated inconsistently.
fix: Add: "While capture is off, `parinn ingest` appends nothing for this node's witnessed runs."

quote: A pin naming no room belongs to its author's principal's personal room on the
problem: This implies a pin can name some other room, and the hub routes principal acts 'in the room it acts on'. Yet Personal room says every event or pin goes there, and no act places a seat anywhere else. The candidate never says whether a device seat may take a create room act for a second room; Device seat exempts only the personal room's create room act.
fix: State in Room act: "Create room is taken only for a node's personal room, the only room; every pin belongs to it."

quote: the CLI or TUI started at a terminal by a process that neither the harness nor
problem: A principal surface is defined only by which process started the CLI or TUI. A run's tool process can bypass that by having a process it did not start launch `parinn` at a pty (a running tmux or screen server, cron, a user service manager), or by sending keys into a TUI the person left open. It can then take widening principal acts: add a constraint pin that restores as the principal's constraint, release a quarantine, or turn capture off. Nothing says what makes the client "authenticated" beyond that ancestry.
fix: Add: "authenticated by the person confirming each widening act there (OWN-02), never by process ancestry alone; a CLI or TUI started or driven on behalf of a run's tool process, through any other process, is never a principal surface."

quote: than ParleyInn's own hook handlers, MCP server and harness strip, is recall: never
problem: The harness strip is exempt from recall. Hook calls from inside a run's tool process are refused, but no rule separates the strip from the same `parinn status --line` that an agent runs in its tool process. That call's output (Health's failures and store locations, which are paths) would reach the model unenveloped and unrecorded. That is a write to an agent outside I2's closed paths.
fix: Define the harness strip as only the status-line call the harness itself makes, and add: "a `parinn status --line` call from a run's tool process or its descendants is recall."

quote: only at a principal surface or through the harness's own plugin install or
problem: An uninstall through the harness's plugin mechanism or the managed install path stops this node recording its runs' events. The candidate makes that a widening principal act 'whatever verb carries it', but only the CLI or TUI at a principal surface can record one, and managed policy may make only cut-only changes. Such an uninstall leaves no recorded act and no capture gap, so events go unrecorded silently, against I1's 'every exception is recorded' and I6.
fix: "Install runs only at a principal surface, through the harness's own plugin install or through the managed install path; uninstall runs only at a principal surface (ADM-02). Hook registrations found removed without that act are counted and shown at ParleyInn's next start as a node-wide capture gap on Runs and Health (I6)."

quote: a hook call from inside a run's tool process is refused and
problem: Principal surface says 'directly or through descendants'; this rule does not, so it is unclear whether a harness that a run's tool process started (an agent running the harness headless) counts as inside. If its hooks are refused, its runs go unrecorded live. If they are accepted, a prompt the agent wrote becomes a trusted `user` event on an `interactive` node.
fix: "a hook call from a run's tool process or any process descending from it is refused and counted, except from a harness it started, whose prompts are recorded as the starting run's `assistant` text, never `user`."

quote: user that signs with this node's device key or a seat key outside ParleyInn's code
problem: R3 covers only signing outside ParleyInn's code. A same-user process (an agent's tool process) needs no key to append a marked `operator` event to the device seat's unsealed tail, and the core's next seal then covers it. The event becomes a sealed principal act, and its constraint pin qualifies and restores. The candidate neither rules this out nor names it as R3.
fix: "A process of the same OS user that writes to the store, or signs with this node's device key or a seat key, outside ParleyInn's code is §6.1's risk R3", or state that the core seals only events it appended itself.

quote: closed path carries only ids, kinds, counts, addresses, key fingerprints and
problem: Nothing bounds 'kinds'. Provenance classes embed names from harness configuration (`mcp:<server>`, `tool_result:<tool>`), which a repository can set to free text, and only tool names and paths are excluded. One implementer may therefore put MCP server names into compaction guidance as trusted text.
fix: Replace 'kinds' with 'kinds (event kinds, seat kinds, pin types, and provenance classes without their `<tool>` or `<server>` names)'.

quote: create room needs none. The room acts are create room, link, pin, edit, unpin.
problem: Create room is a general room act that needs no capability, so a principal could create a room other than the personal room. Such a room has no use: no act adds a seat to it, runs get seats only in the personal room, "every event or pin goes" to the personal room, so nothing there restores or can be recalled. Two implementers will differ on whether `parinn room create` exists and what it does.
fix: State that create room is taken only once per node, by the device seat at ParleyInn's first start, creating that node's personal room, and that any other create room act is refused and counted (I6).

quote: or derived artifact from recall and restore blocks, on the node that records it, without deletion (I5).
problem: In this candidate, derived artifacts (indexes, room state, trust levels, run and integrity statuses, quarantine set) have no content of their own that recall returns apart from their events, and restore blocks hold none of them. Quarantining a derived artifact therefore has no defined effect, and I5 also names it as a target.
fix: Remove "or derived artifact" from Quarantine and from I5, or name which derived artifacts can be quarantined and what that takes out of recall.
